title: Mars Rover Maze
rule1: To get out of a maze, touch the **right wall with your right hand** and keep walking without lifting your hand. You will go around every dead end and always find the exit, whatever maze you are in.
rule2: Build a program from blocks. The rover can only see what is **straight ahead**, so your algorithm has to work with that sensor. When the program is ready, press “New maze”: the right algorithm will lead the rover through any maze.
noEditorText: The block editor couldn’t be loaded. Refresh the page. If that doesn’t help, tell your teacher.
fieldAria: A 10 by 10 maze on the surface of Mars
hint1: Idea: imagine walking through the maze with your right hand always touching the wall on your right. Your hand “guides” you along the wall and always leads you to the exit.
hint2: First try turning right. While there is a wall ahead, turn left. When the way is clear, drive forward. Keep repeating this until the rover is at the finish.
hint3Code:
repeat while [ ??? ]

streakTitle: In a row without mistakes: {n} of 3
ready: Build a program from blocks and press “Run”.
running: The rover is on its way…
stopped: Stopped. The rover is back at the start.
resetDone: The rover is at the start. Same maze, program unchanged.
changed: The program was changed, so the run was stopped.
newMazeSay: New maze. Same program: try it out here.
linkMazeSay: Opened the maze from the link. Same program.
emptyLoose: The blocks aren’t attached to “▶ when started” (they are grey). Drag them under the start block until they snap on.
emptyProgram: The program is empty. Drag blocks from the left under “▶ when started”.
winNew: Finish! The rover is at the base. Now press “New maze”: will this program work in another one too?
winAgain: Finish! But this maze has already been counted. Press “New maze” and test your algorithm on a different one.
bump: Boom! There’s a wall ahead. Check the condition before moving.
limit: It looks like the rover is going in circles. Think about how to always keep to the right wall.
end: The program ended, but the rover isn’t at the finish yet.
modalText: One and the same program guided the rover through 3 different mazes. This is how real algorithms work: they solve a whole class of problems, not just one.
tt.start: The start of the program. The blocks under it run from top to bottom.
tt.forward: Drive one cell forward. If there is a wall ahead, the rover will bump into it.
tt.while: Run the blocks inside while the condition is true
tt.if: Run the blocks inside if the condition is true
tt.ifelse: If the condition is true, run the first blocks, otherwise run the second ones
